4. That Pre-emptor-Respondent-side, thereafter, by way of an amendment dated 16.05.1996 put forth the case that heirs of Yukub Ali Munshi had shown transfer in respect of an area of 3 kanis, two (2) gondas two (2) karas and two (2) krantees equivalent to 3.76 acres out of land of disputed Cadastral Survey Khatian Nos. 17 and 18, 19, 20 and 21 along with khas khatian No. 1 and schedule of sale deed had shown that Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 meant for transfer of 2.63 acres of land and pre-emptee-petitioner got no interest in respect of case holding. The Pre-emptor-respondents are co-sharers by way of inheritance and also by purchase. 

 9. Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the petitions submits that though land of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 18-21 had been shown as tenanted land in the sale deed dated 17.04.1926 under Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 but the said under-tenancies subsequently got no existence as under tenancies and the said land went to khas holding of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 and those land of under-tenancies stood recorded in State Acquisition Khatian No. 10 in the names of tenants or heirs of transferors of Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 17 and not in the names of heirs of any under tenants of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 18-21 and the deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 is a positive proof that Karim Uddin and his three (3) brothers purchased 3.76 acres of land from sons of Yakub Ali and Karim Uddin got .94 acres of land in the case holding and pre-emptee-Petitioner inherited .18¾ acres of land from his father Karimuddin and pre-emptee-Petitioner still remains owner and co-sharer by way of inheritance in respect of .1¾ acres of land after transfer of .17 acres of land and pre-emptee-Petitioner having been a co-sharer by way of inheritance, pre-emption cases by Pre-emptor-Respondent is not at all maintainable and both the Trail Court and the Lower Appellate Court concurrently found that the Pre-emptee-Petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance and those findings rested upon correct construction and reading of the sale deed dated 17.04.1926, share of Yakub Ali in the Case holding and materials on record but the learned Single Judge of High Court Division totally misdirected himself in his approach in resolving the legal battle involved in Pre-emption cases and committed a substantial error in holding that pre-emptee-Petitioner inherited .13 acres of land and transferred .17 acres of land and thereby exhausted all his interest in case holding and became a stranger and this Hon'ble Division did not at all explore the legal controversy and in a summary way dismissed the leave petitions and Judgment under challenge in Civil Review petition may kindly be reviewed in the interest of Justice.
